figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Classification of terpenoid saccharide family natural products and retrobiosynthetic analysis of cosmosporaside C (1). a) Cyclic terpenoid-
cyclic saccharide (cT-cS). b) Linear terpenoid-cyclic saccharide (lT-cS). c) Cyclic terpenoid-linear saccharide polyol (cT-lSP). d) Linear terpenoid-
linear saccharide polyol (lT-lSP). e) Retrobiosynthetic analysis shows that 1 is possibly derived from 2 through multiple tailoring steps, such as
oxidation, acetylation, prenylation and glycosylation, the key enzyme(s) responsible for 2 synthesis via primary central metabolites is unknown.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Confirmation of the cos gene cluster and gene knockout of
cosA in F. orthoceras. a) Organization and proposed function of cos
cluster. b) LC–MS analyses show that 1 is produced by F. orthoceras but
missing in the cosA knockout mutant of F. orthoceras.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Analysis and confirmation of the CosA function. a) Sequence similarity network (SSN) analysis shows that CosA and its homologous
proteins are classified into a separate clade (shown in red). b) Phylogenetic tree analysis indicates that CosA and its homologues are different from
the well-known meroterpene family UbiA-type PTs. Ft-CosA (KAH7245299.1), Fa-CosA (KAH6954421.1), Foxy-CosA (XP018252515.1), Fv-CosA
(RBR19905.1), and ColA (RDW88428.1) are homologues of CosA from F. tricinctum, F. avenaceum, F. oxysporum, F. verticillioides, and Coleophoma
cylindrospora, respectively. c) LC–MS analyses of the culture extracts from heterologously expressed cosA and its mutation in A. nidulans. d) HPLC
analyses of the saccharide polyol hydrolysate from 2.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Substrate confirmation of CosA. a) LC–MS analyses of heterologously expressed cosA, mpdh and m1pase (from A. nidulans) in S. cerevisiae.
b) Saccharide polyol metabolism is involved in the synthesis of 2. GK: glucokinase, GPI: phosphoglucose isomerase, MPDH: mannitol-1-phosphate
dehydrogenase, M1Pase: mannitol-1-phosphate phosphatase, MtDH: mannitol dehydrogenase, FK: fructokinase. c) Gene knockout of mpdh,
m1pase and mtdh in AN-cosA shows the importance of MPDH and M1Pase for 2 synthesis. d) 13C6-D-Man incorporation in different strains
confirms that the de novo synthesis of D-Man1p by the MPDH-catalyzed pathway is essential for 2 synthesis. The extracted ion chromatograms
(EICs) of m/z 409 [M+Na]+ and m/z 415 [M+Na]+ are for 2 and 13C6-2, respectively.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. The functions of CosB and CosC and confirmation of the absolute configuration of 3. a) LC–MS analyses of the culture extracts from
heterologously expressed cosAB and cosABC in A. nidulans. b) Compound 4 was converted into 5a and 5b in A. nidulans, or into 3 by CosC-
catalyzed epoxide opening. c) The proposed mechanism for 3 in the synthesis of 3a and 3b during the acid hydrolysis process. d) The MTPA-
derived esters of 3a.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. The function, tailoring timing, and substrate tolerance of CosD and CosE. a) LC–MS analyses of the culture extracts from heterologously
expressed cosABCD, cosABCE, and cosABCDE in A. nidulans. b) Time course competition assays of CosD toward 3 and 7. c) Time course
competition assays of CosE toward 3 and 6. d) Routes for the transformation of 3 into 8. e) Diagram of the substrate tolerance assay of CosD and
CosE. f) CosE utilizes C4/6/8-CoA to acylate 3, yielding 7a, 7b, and 7c. g) CosD recognizes 7a, 7b, and 7c to form the C5 prenylation products 8a,
8b, and 8c, respectively. The extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) of m/z 529 [M+Na]+, m/z 557 [M+Na]+, m/z 585 [M+Na]+, m/z 597 [M
+Na]+, m/z 625 [M+Na]+ and m/z 653 [M+Na]+ in (f,g) are for 7a, 7b, 7c, 8a, 8b, and 8c, respectively.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 7. The functional confirmation of CosF. a) Gene knockout and
overexpression of cosF in F. orthoceras show its ability to catalyze
mannosylation of 8 to yield 1. b) LC–MS analyses of the culture extracts
from heterologously expressed cosABCDEF in A. nidulans.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 8
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 8. The proposed biosynthetic pathway for 1 shows complex assembly machinery used for the syntheses of hybrid terpenoid saccharide
cosmosporasides.
